input.$description: Single-line text field. sm has no floating label — the placeholder simply vanishes on focus/when typing, same text stays 16px throughout (see $description on size.sm). base/lg float the placeholder into a 12px label above the value on focus or once populated. Value/placeholder text is 16px at every size, deliberately — Safari on iOS auto-zooms the page on focus if an input's font-size is under 16px; going smaller (e.g. matching the button's 14px body size) would trigger that on every mobile focus.

sm.$description: 32px. No floating label — the box isn't tall enough to hold a 12px label + 16px value stacked and still read as anything but cramped. Placeholder disappears the moment the field is focused or has a value, same as a plain unlabeled input.

base.$description: 40px, the default size. Floating label: 12px, sitting directly above the 16px value with 0 gap between their line-boxes and 2px from the stack to the field's own top/bottom edges — vertically centered via flexbox rather than hand-computed padding, since 12px/16px text at leading.tight doesn't sum to a value that divides evenly into 40px, and flex-centering doesn't need it to.

lg.$description: 48px. Same 12px floating label as base, but with 4px between the label and value line-boxes and 4px from the stack to the field's top/bottom edges — more breathing room at the larger size. Same flex-centering approach as base.

default.$description: Empty, not focused. surface.sunken + border.default are each already documented ('Inputs...recessed' / 'input borders at rest') from the semantic-color session, before this component existed.

hover.$description: border.strong's own token description already says 'input border on hover' — written before this component existed.

focus.$description: Floating label (base/lg only) turns brand-blue while focused — reverts to text.muted once blurred, even if still populated, so blue always means 'this is the active field', not 'this field has a value'.

populated.$description: Has a value, not focused — the base/lg floating label stays up (that's a layout state, not a color one) but every color reverts to default. Named 'populated' rather than 'filled' to avoid colliding with the unrelated fill.* token family.

disabled.$description: surface.disabled and surface.sunken are both {color.gray.100} — same value, same pattern as fill.disabled==fill.neutral on the secondary button. Disabled doesn't change the background, only the text/icon/label fading out.

error.$description: Scoped to the field's own border only — a separate helper/error-message text element below the field isn't built here, wasn't asked for.
